description: Guided, searchable examples for inspecting paths and working safely with files and folders in PowerShell.

actionDescriptions.Get: Read or enumerate existing file-system content without changing it.
actionDescriptions.Test: Evaluate a path condition and return a Boolean result.
actionDescriptions.New: Create a new file-system item at a deliberate location.

objectDescriptions.ChildItem: Files, folders, and other children beneath a provider path.
objectDescriptions.Content: The text or data stored inside a file.
objectDescriptions.Path: A file-system or provider location whose existence can be checked.
objectDescriptions.Item: A file, folder, registry key, or another provider-backed object.

commands.name: Get-ChildItem
commands.description: List files and folders at a selected path.
commands.definition: Enumerates child items from a PowerShell provider location. With the FileSystem provider, the returned objects retain metadata such as name, full path, size, and modification time for later pipeline operations.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The directory or provider path to enumerate.

parameters.name: Recurse
parameters.description: Include descendants beneath the selected path.

examples.title: List PowerShell files recursively
examples.explanation: The command starts at the current directory, descends into child folders, and returns only files matching the .ps1 filter. No file-system content is modified.

commands.name: Get-Content
commands.description: Read file content into the PowerShell pipeline.
commands.definition: Reads content from a provider item. Text files normally produce one string per line, allowing downstream commands to filter, transform, count, or export the data without first writing a custom parser.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The file whose content should be read.

parameters.name: Raw
parameters.description: Return the entire file as one string instead of one object per line.

examples.title: Read a JSON document as one string
examples.explanation: Raw mode preserves the document as a single string, which can then be passed directly to ConvertFrom-Json for structured access.

commands.name: Test-Path
commands.description: Check whether a path exists before using it.
commands.definition: Evaluates a provider path and returns True or False. It is useful for guard conditions before reading, copying, moving, or creating content, and can distinguish containers from leaf items with PathType.

parameters.name: PathType
parameters.description: Optionally require Any, Container, or Leaf semantics.

examples.title: Read a configuration only when present
examples.explanation: The condition confirms that settings.json exists as a file before Get-Content attempts to read it, avoiding a predictable missing-path error.

commands.name: New-Item
commands.description: Create a new file or folder at a selected path.
commands.definition: Creates a provider-backed item. In the FileSystem provider, ItemType controls whether the result is a file or directory. Existing destinations require an explicit conflict decision rather than being silently replaced by this guide.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The full path of the new item.

parameters.name: ItemType
parameters.description: The item kind, commonly File or Directory for file-system paths.

examples.title: Create a project output directory
examples.explanation: The guard prevents a conflict when the directory already exists; New-Item runs only when the output folder is absent.
